summary.headline: Supreme Petrochem Q4 FY26 standalone revenue INR 1,587 crore (+3% YoY), operating EBITDA INR 253 crore at 15.9% margin; ABS running at ~65% of design capacity.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 3% YoY to INR 1,587 crore on higher volumes (100,664 t, +5.4% YoY) and better spreads, with operating EBITDA up 75% YoY to INR 253 crore (15.9% margin) and PAT of INR 168 crore. FY26 revenue fell 11% to INR 5,338 crore on a ~17% lower average styrene monomer price, while volumes grew ~2% to 363,203 t. Styrene spiked in March 2026 on the West Asia conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, creating inventory-gain/loss uncertainty management could not quantify. The mass ABS plant restarted at ~65% of design capacity after an equipment failure, and EPS Phase-II (Amdoshi) lifted capacity to 115,000 tpa in April 2026. The company remains debt-free with INR 700 crore investable surplus.

segments.name: Polystyrene / EPS
segments.commentary: EPS capacity raised from 85,000 tpa to 115,000 tpa at Amdoshi with EPS Phase-II commissioned on 14 April 2026. Management flagged EPS exports to Europe as a new outlet; de-bottlenecking of PS under evaluation with no timeline given.

segments.name: ABS
segments.commentary: Mass ABS plant restarted at ~65% of design capacity after an equipment failure; effective capacity cut to ~45,000 t from 70,000 t for now. Phase-II targeted by FY28 but not confirmed.

segments.name: SPC / Xmold compounding
segments.commentary: Management targets ~50,000 t compounding volume by FY28 (if not FY27) and expects Xmold utilisation of ~65-70% in FY27 vs ~45-50% in FY26. Two AC manufacturers onboarded in Sri City.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guidance of 8-10%, conditional on normalcy by June-end/Q2 FY27.
ABS utilisation expected at ~80-90% of the 65%-operating-level capacity this year; ABS FY27 volume target ~36,000 t referenced in analyst question.
FY27 company-wide capex of ~INR 250 crore; Haryana PS/EPS spend deferred until IOC styrene plant timing is clear.
No volume guidance for ABS and base volumes separately beyond the 8-10% total.
Management declined to estimate Q1 FY27 EBITDA; said normalised conditions would yield better results than FY26.
Final dividend INR 8 per share; total FY26 dividend INR 10.5 per share (face value INR 2).
capex_capacity: EPS Phase-II at Amdoshi commissioned 14 April 2026, EPS capacity 85,000 tpa to 115,000 tpa.
Mass ABS plant at ~65% of design capacity pending restoration of impacted equipment; capacity temporarily ~45,000 t vs original 70,000 t.
ABS Phase-II targeted by FY28; management said it is still aiming for it but no firm commitment.
PS de-bottlenecking under evaluation; management said the new line was set up ~3 years ago and gave no timeline (analyst's 'April 2027-28' not confirmed).
Haryana: no big PS/EPS spend until IOC styrene monomer plant commissioning date clarity; only infrastructure spend this year.
demand_pricing: Styrene monomer rose from ~$1,000/t pre-conflict to a peak of ~$1,650-1,700/t in March 2026; now ~$1,500/t.
Management said it is not entering new OEM contracts while prices are volatile; OEMs continue to buy at current prices.
Non-OEM demand hit in April by high prices, labour shortage and gas supply constraints; OEM/non-OEM split cited as roughly 50:50 or 45:55.

Commodity PS pricing is linked to landed import price plus premium; management said there is no threat from ABS imports at current landed prices (~INR 230/kg at INR 95/USD for ABS booked at $2,300-2,400).
Management cited a PS-SM GP spread moving from ~$200/t to ~$275/t; said spreads are hard to define given daily price changes.
Zero import duty on PS, ABS and SM following government decision, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Can inventory gains/losses be quantified and when will they be booked?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is next to impossible to estimate; gains/losses are booked as material is sold, with no separate inventory-gain entry.

qa_highlights.question: Is ABS at 65% of capacity the new normal and what are FY27 volume targets?
qa_highlights.answer: ABS capacity at 65% pending equipment repair; FY27 guidance is 8-10% volume growth if normal by June-end. Exports to Europe slowed due to Cape of Good Hope routing.

qa_highlights.question: Can ABS and PS demand from non-OEM be quantified in April/May?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to quantify; non-OEM demand impacted from April, with OEM/non-OEM split about 45-50% OEM.

qa_highlights.question: Styrene and ACN sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: China has its own production and is exporting surplus; company has ACN stock and is sourcing from other geographies; some styrene sourced from Asia and China.

qa_highlights.question: Trading share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Trading was ~18% of Q4 revenue and expected to be 18-19% for FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a PS de-bottlenecking plan and spread outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Evaluating de-bottlenecking with no timeline; GP spread moved to ~$275/t from ~$200/t, but management said it is volatile.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cash flow and debtors of INR 520 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher selling prices, higher ABS volumes and higher inventory raised working capital; management expects it to normalise.

risks_watch: Inventory loss risk when styrene prices fall after normalisation; management cannot quantify it.
ABS equipment repair timeline and whether capacity returns from 65% to higher levels; Phase-II timing by FY28.
Non-OEM demand erosion from high prices, labour and gas shortages; OEM contracts not yet re-signed.
Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption and styrene supply availability; export logistics via Cape of Good Hope.
Haryana PS/EPS expansion contingent on IOC styrene plant commissioning.
Working capital build (debtors INR 520 crore) and cash-flow normalisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet, dividend and EPS commissioning, but evasive and cautious on pricing, inventory gains/losses, Q1 FY27 and volume guidance, repeatedly citing a fluid situation. Management declined to quantify several items (inventory impact, ABS-EPS spreads, April/May demand).

growth.why: Management guides 8-10% FY27 volume growth (midpoint 9%), conditional on normalcy by June/July, backed by EPS Phase-II (85k to 115k tpa, commissioned 14 April 2026) and ABS restart toward 80-90% of ~45k t effective capacity, but the Haryana PS/EPS spend is deferred and ABS Phase-II is unconfirmed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: PS-SM GP spread rose from ~$200/t to ~$275/t and management said normalised conditions would beat FY26, but inventory gains/losses cannot be quantified and FY26 operating EBITDA margin was only ~9.6% (INR 515 crore on INR 5,338 crore).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: EPS capacity already rose 85,000 to 115,000 tpa (commissioned 14 April 2026, +35%), and ABS is being restored from ~45,000 t effective toward 70,000 t design, with ABS Phase-II targeted by FY28 but not confirmed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 8-10% FY27 volume growth (midpoint 9%) on EPS Phase-II (+30,000 tpa) and ABS restoration to 80-90% of ~45,000 t effective capacity, though it is conditional on normalcy by June/Q2 FY27 and Q4 FY26 volume was already +5.4% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: next 2-4 quarters, conditional on IOC styrene plant timing
rows.why: Company-wide FY27 capex is only ~INR 250 crore and Haryana PS/EPS spend is deferred, but the company has INR 700 crore investable surplus and utilisation is only ~65%, so a larger announcement is conditional rather than imminent.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no upgrade and its tone on Q1 FY27 and volumes was cautious, with the ABS plant at ~65% of design and non-OEM demand already hit from April.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 8-10% volume growth is conditional on normalcy by June-end/Q2 FY27, and management declined to estimate Q1 FY27 EBITDA amid styrene at ~$1,500/t after a $1,650-1,700 peak.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: EPS exports to Europe are a new outlet and two AC manufacturers were onboarded in Sri City for SPC/Xmold, but no product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Xmold/SPC utilisation ramp to 65-70% in FY27
rows.why: Xmold utilisation is expected at 65-70% in FY27 vs 45-50% in FY26, and two AC manufacturers were onboarded in Sri City.

rows.label: Debt-free balance sheet with INR 700 crore investable surplus
rows.why: The company is debt-free with INR 700 crore investable surplus, which funds any future expansion without borrowing.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation after debtor build
rows.why: Debtors reached INR 520 crore on higher prices and ABS volumes, and management expects working capital to normalise, but this is not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on the balance sheet, dividend and EPS Phase-II commissioning, but cautious and evasive on styrene pricing, inventory gains/losses, Q1 FY27 EBITDA and April/May non-OEM demand, while analysts pushed on the ABS repair timeline, Phase-II timing and PS de-bottlenecking.
